PACK.scope: All source videos, transcript sidecars, slide decks/pages, and confidently mapped historical question-source pages available for Engineering Mechanics 1, Unit_02 (UNIT 2); missing bucket material is reported as a gap.
PACK.title: UE26ME142A · Unit_02 — UNIT 2 · Complete Unit Master
PACK.subtitle: Notes-first study master · source-cited lecture explanations and compact page takeaways
PACK.compiled_from: Hugging Face PESU_Materials source tree, official units.json catalogue, transcript sidecars, slide text/PDF/PPT sources and the selected First_Year_8enterprise archive; see the provenance datasets in the release ZIP.
PACK.how_to_use: Read the edited lesson notes by topic. Evidence chips point to transcript intervals and slide pages. The complete source transcripts, page text, formula candidates, and image locators are preserved in sibling JSON datasets.
PACK.pyq_note: Historical question-source excerpts are shown only when a page has a strong text-based unit match. They are source references, not new solutions or exam predictions.
PACK.figure_note: Source figures are full-page renderings of the original slide deck pages. Their exact page text appears separately for search and copying; image-only pages are labelled.
PACK.symbols_remark: No formula candidate is asserted as mathematically verified solely from OCR/transcript text. See datasets/content-index.json for raw candidates and source locators.
PACK.coverage_note: This master retains the source content and provenance for the official unit. It is a DRAFT pending human page-level review; see PACK.gaps and the QA report.
tag_legend: Verbatim or OCR-derived text, kept separate from editorial notes.

Unit map · UE26ME142A · Unit_02: UNIT 2

Official catalogue entry: UE26ME142A, Unit_02 (UNIT 2). Bucket folder present: yes. Videos: 15; slide decks: 18.

Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

My name is Dr.

Key details

  • SV Venkatish from Civil Engineering and the Department of Science and Humanities PS University.
  • Two chapters which are there in unit one, chapter one and chapter two.
  • In chapter one, we had discussed a few of the definitions and the units of forces.
  • In chapter two, we had four topics.
  • One as resolution of forces.
  • In that you have rectangular components, N and T components, then axes which are not at 90 degrees, then the difference between projection and components.
  • That's topic one under chapter two.
  • The second topic was on movement.
  • We discussed moment, varingance principle, and we have solved problems on moment also.
  • That's second topic.
  • The third topic was on couple.
  • We have seen what is the definition of couple, characteristics of couple, classification of couple, effects of couple, and very importantly, what do you mean by force couple system?
  • And then we have solved problems on that.
  • The last topic in unit one, chapter two, is resulted.
  • We have discussed what is resulted, how do we determine the characteristics of resultant, four characteristics that is magnitude, direction, sense, and point of application.
  • To determine the point of application, we have used principle of moments, okay, and then we have solved problems on that.
  • To certain extent unit 3 also.
  • You have the background of unit one.
  • We will now get into unit two.
  • And the prescribed textbook that we are using is engineering mechanics statics.
  • Very importantly, it is the eighth edition, which is in SI version.
  • And the author is Miriam Craig and adopted by Bolton.
  • There's one more in this other than equilibrium, we also have trusses.
  • We will discuss that later when we take up that topic.
  • So first we will discuss about chapter three, which is equilibrium.
  • What is equilibrium?
  • If the resultant force and the resultant movement acting on a body on which there are several.
  • Forces and moments acting, that is a system of forces are acting.
  • If the resultant force and moment both of them are zero, then we say that the body is in equilibrium.
  • Application of the force would be a rotatory motion which will make this body to rotate.
  • It won't move.
  • But you can also have a combination of transmitter motion as well as rotatory motion.
  • It ensures that there is no transmitter emotion.
  • Why I'm saying this?
  • Because as you could see, the net force because of a couple is zero.
  • But what is the effect of a couple?
  • It makes the body to rotate.
  • It should not get displaced, it should not rotate also.
  • But if we take this, m is equal to 0, or algebraic sum of all the moments of all the forces at any point, at any point should be equal to 0.
  • This will ensure that there is no rotatory motion.

These are edited study notes based on the cited lecture interval. Check uncertain speech recognition against the source transcript and recording.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

Ensure or to show that the body is in equilibrium or to determine the forces which makes the body to be in equilibrium.

Key details

  • What is that?
  • The first thing is a free body diagram.
  • We have already discussed about free body diagram.
  • But since it comes exclusively in this chapter, I am again arbitrating or bringing the concept of a free body diagram.
